name: J.B. Pritzker
current_role: Governor of Illinois (re-elected to a third term on Nov 3, 2026)
profile: Hyatt hotel-fortune heir who co-founded Pritzker Group (private equity/venture) with brother Anthony and ran it until 2017. Elected Illinois governor in 2018, re-elected 2022 and won a rare third term in Nov 2026, beating Darren Bailey again; widely discussed as a possible 2028 presidential candidate.
interesting_fact: He is the first Democrat elected to three terms as Illinois governor and the first governor of either party to win a third term since Jim Thompson in the 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Before politics he founded 1871 (2012), the Merchandise Mart startup incubator run by the Chicagoland Entrepreneurial Center and named for the rebuilding after the 1871 Chicago Fire; it was later ranked the world's top private business incubator (UBI Global, 2019).

public_contacts.value: alex.gough@illinois.gov (Press Secretary, Office of the Governor)

notes: Sitting governor; podcast requests best via the governor's scheduling-request form or press office. Strong fit for entrepreneurship angle (1871, Pritzker Group VC) and Illinois data-center/energy policy.

name: Jacob Brunsborg
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Lars Larsen Group (owner of JYSK)
profile: Son of JYSK founder Lars Larsen; became chairman of Lars Larsen Group (JYSK, ILVA, Actona, investments) in June 2019 shortly before his father's death. Rose through JYSK as head of purchasing and brand director, then did business development, entrepreneurship and board work; now steers the group's strategy, including investments in securities, property and green energy.
interesting_fact: He carries his mother's surname rather than Larsen, and his father reportedly warned him against aiming for the JYSK CEO job, insisting management be chosen on merit while ownership stays in the family.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1993 as a trainee ('elev') in the JYSK store on Grenåvej in Aarhus, and did his military service with the Royal Danish Life Guards (Dronningens Livregiment).

public_contacts.value: Press contact: Communications Director Lise Brøndum Wemmelund via Lars Larsen Group press room

notes: Rarely gives interviews and says he is less outgoing than his father (lex.dk). Group invests in green energy, a possible hook. Approach via the group's Communications Director.

name: Jiang Nanchun (Jason Jiang)
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Focus Media (Shenzhen-listed 002027)
profile: Shanghai-based founder of Focus Media, China's largest elevator/building-lobby digital-screen advertising network. Took it public on Nasdaq in 2005, delisted in 2013 and relisted in Shenzhen via reverse takeover in 2016; he still runs the company and is a prominent voice on brand-building in China.
interesting_fact: Focus Media began in 2003 with an offbeat idea: selling ads on screens in office-building elevator lobbies, a format nobody then knew was worth anything.
deep_cut_fact: A Chinese literature graduate of East China Normal University, he wanted to be a poet; he credits student poetry for his business instincts: 'Writing poems requires you to connect and combine two seemingly irrelevant objects with a sharp imagination, which is also true in business.'
notes: Comfortable public speaker (NYU Shanghai, CKGSB alumnus events). Outreach likely needs to go via Focus Media IR/marketing in Chinese.

name: William (Bill) Stone
current_role: Chairman and CEO, SS&C Technologies Holdings (Nasdaq: SSNC)
profile: Evansville, Indiana native and former KPMG director who founded SS&C (Securities Software & Consulting) in 1986 with ~$20,000 of savings. Took it public in 1996, private in 2005 and public again in 2011; built it via acquisitions (DST, Intralinks, Black Diamond) into a major fund-administration and financial-software firm, which he still runs as its largest individual shareholder.
interesting_fact: During the dot-com bust SS&C shrank from 610 to 250 employees (June 1999-Dec 2001) before Stone rebuilt it, partly by adding data-center and outsourced services.
deep_cut_fact: He started SS&C in the basement of his Connecticut home after a career that began in 1977 as a KPMG auditor in St. Louis and included running special investment services at broker-dealer Advest; the firm had 4 employees, 17 that year, 38 by 1988. Earlier he captained Reitz Memorial High's football team in Evansville.
notes: Company-level contacts only; route via Prosek Partners. SS&C operates large data centers, good tie-in to podcast themes.

name: Isabella Seràgnoli
current_role: President (chair) and sole shareholder, Coesia S.p.A., Bologna
profile: Sole owner of Coesia, the Bologna packaging-machinery group that grew out of G.D (founded 1923, taken over by her father Enzo), whose cigarette-packing machines dominated the tobacco industry. She took over in 2002, renamed it Coesia in 2005 and diversified into many packaging sectors, while funding major Bologna philanthropy (MAST, hospices).
interesting_fact: She founded MAST (Manifattura di Arti, Sperimentazione e Tecnologia) in Bologna, a combined corporate-welfare and cultural centre known for its photography exhibitions on industry and work.
deep_cut_fact: Her family's hospice foundation funded and built 'L'Arca sull'albero', Bologna's paediatric palliative-care hospice opened in 2024, designed by Renzo Piano to sit suspended among trees in a purpose-planted wood.
notes: Very private; rarely interviewed. Best route is Coesia press office. Coesia's Corporate Governance page lists her as President with Alessandro Parimbelli as CEO.

name: Nikhil Kamath
current_role: Co-founder, Zerodha; founder of True Beacon and Gruhas; host of the 'WTF is' podcast
profile: Bengaluru entrepreneur who co-founded discount brokerage Zerodha with brother Nithin in 2010, disrupting Indian retail broking. Also runs zero-fee asset manager True Beacon, co-founded investment firm Gruhas (2021), and hosts the 'WTF is' podcast, whose guests have included PM Narendra Modi, Bill Gates and Elon Musk.
interesting_fact: In 2023 he became the youngest Indian signatory of the Giving Pledge, committing to give away at least half his wealth.
deep_cut_fact: A school dropout after 10th grade with no formal degree, he started out working in a call centre while trading equities on the side; in 2024 he launched WTFund, a non-dilutive grant fund for founders aged 25 and under.
notes: Fellow podcaster; peer-to-peer pitch (guest swap) is a natural angle. Very active on X/Instagram. Gruhas invests in climate tech. No published press email found.

name: Jonathan Harmsworth (4th Viscount Rothermere)
current_role: Chairman, Daily Mail and General Trust (DMGT)
profile: Fourth-generation Harmsworth to run the Daily Mail empire; became chairman of DMGT in 1998 on his father's death. Built MailOnline into one of the world's most-read news sites, took DMGT private in 2021 (~£1.6bn), and in Nov 2025 agreed a £500m deal to buy The Telegraph, which faced a UK public-interest/competition review from Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: DMGT owned energy-market data firm Genscape (bought 2006 for ~$130m) and sold it to Verisk/Wood Mackenzie in 2019 for $364m, a useful energy-data angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Educated at Gordonstoun in Scotland, he went to university in the US, studying history at Duke University, before joining the family's Associated Newspapers.
notes: Very private, rarely interviewed. Telegraph deal status after the 2026 regulatory review not confirmed here; check before outreach. Route via DMGT PR.

name: Maximilian Rudolph von Finck
current_role: Heir/investor in the von Finck family fortune; board member of family holding Clair (per Bilanz)
profile: Middle son (b. c.1969) of the late Bavarian banker-investor August von Finck Jr. (d. Nov 2021), whose fortune included a large SGS (testing/inspection) stake, mostly sold in 2020 ahead of an equal four-way inheritance. Naturalised Swiss (canton Schwyz); Bilanz reports he is mainly active as an entrepreneur in the USA, e.g. in the seed business.
interesting_fact: The family sold SGS shares worth about CHF 2.3bn in 2020, reportedly to split a holding too big to divide equally among August von Finck Jr.'s four children.
notes: Extremely private; almost no public profile and no published contact. Identity matched to the von Finck SGS fortune via Bilanz, but his own business activities are not documented. Hurun listing likely reflects inherited share of the family fortune. Not a realistic podcast target.

name: The Lazari family
current_role: Owners of Lazari (Lazari Investments, Lazari Financial Holdings, Lazari Developments), Mayfair, London
profile: Family of the late Greek-Cypriot developer Chris (Christos) Lazari (d. 2015), who founded Lazari Investments in 1976. Widow Maritsa (co-founder) and children run a private group with 2.9m sq ft of prime London property and combined assets of over £4.1bn across eight London estates, including the West End and Euston Road.
interesting_fact: The group is now three businesses: the legacy property company, a property-finance lender and a development arm, with combined assets above £4.1bn.
deep_cut_fact: Founder Chris Lazari left Cyprus at 16 with just £20 aboard the MV Messapia, washed dishes and waited tables to study fashion design, and built the 'Drendie Girl' high-street clothing label before moving into property in 1978.
notes: Family entry: founder Chris Lazari died 2015; widow Maritsa (b. 1943) is alive per Wikipedia, and children are directors. Low-profile family; best route is FTI Consulting.

name: Joseph Edelman
current_role: Founder, CEO and Portfolio Manager, Perceptive Advisors (New York)
profile: Biotech-focused hedge fund manager who founded Perceptive Advisors in July 1999 with $6m; it grew to about $10bn under management. A former sell-side biotech analyst (Prudential Securities) and Aries Fund manager at Paramount Capital, he also backed the ARYA biotech SPACs and sits on the New York Genome Center board.
interesting_fact: After a rough 2021-22, his flagship Perceptive Life Sciences fund returned about 83% in 2025 on biotech winners like Praxis Precision Medicines and Celcuity.
deep_cut_fact: A UC San Diego psychology graduate (magna cum laude, 1978) and son of a Columbia biochemist, he quit pharmacology grad school, moved to New York, and worked as assistant comptroller for the Actors' Equity Association to pay for his NYU Stern MBA.
notes: Low media profile; firm-level contact only. Fit with podcast is weaker (biotech, not energy/data centers).

name: Richard M. DeVos
profile: Richard Marvin 'Rich' DeVos, co-founder of Amway and owner of the Orlando Magic (the 1997 Forbes listing matches him). Died September 6, 2018, aged 92, in Ada, Michigan.
notes: Deceased (source: https://money.cnn.com/2018/09/06/news/amway-richard-devos/index.html ; NBA.com obituary). Not to be confused with his son Dick DeVos (Richard M. DeVos Jr.), former Amway president.

name: K.C. Liu (Liu Ko-chen)
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Advantech (TWSE: 2395); becomes full-time Chairman on Jan 1, 2027 when Miller Chang takes over as CEO
profile: Co-founded Advantech in 1983 at 29 with two HP Taiwan colleagues and built it into the world's largest industrial PC maker (about 41% share), now pushing edge-AI and IoT platforms. In 2026 he announced succession: from 2027 he will focus on governance, long-term development and new business investments.
interesting_fact: An avid reader of management books, he shares titles such as Built to Last and Blue Ocean Strategy with Advantech staff.
deep_cut_fact: Before Advantech he was an R&D engineer and then a sales engineer in HP Taiwan's Instrument Department; in 2026 he noted he had spent 42 years building the company since co-founding it at 29.
notes: Strong fit: industrial edge-AI/IoT hardware used in energy and data-center infrastructure. Leadership transition on Jan 1, 2027 is a timely hook.

name: Emad Al Muhaidib
current_role: Vice Chairman, Al Muhaidib Group (Dammam, Saudi Arabia)
profile: Co-owner (about 28%) and vice chairman of Al Muhaidib Group, the family conglomerate founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir as a food trader, later spanning building materials, real estate, infrastructure, consumer goods and finance, with stakes in at least 16 listed Saudi and Egyptian companies. He leads the group's development in Saudi Arabia's Western Province.
interesting_fact: Al Muhaidib Group started in 1943 when his father Abdulkadir traded food, before expanding into building materials and real estate; Emad and brothers Essam and Sulaiman took over after his death in 1996.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond the family group he sits on the boards of Middle East Paper Company, Thabat Construction, Waste Collection and Recycling Co (WASCO) and United Feed, and is vice president of the Economic and Social Committee of the Emirate of Makkah Province.
notes: Low public profile; group-level contact only. Brothers Sulaiman (chairs Savola, vice-chairs Almarai) and Essam (CEO) are the group's more public faces.

name: Daniel Lubetzky
current_role: Founder of KIND Snacks; founder of family office Camino Partners; Shark Tank 'shark'; founder of Starts With Us
profile: Mexico City-born, Stanford Law-trained entrepreneur who founded KIND in 2004 and sold it to Mars (deal valuing it at ~$5bn in 2020); he sold his remaining stake in 2025. Now invests via Camino Partners (consumer health, longevity, CPG), is a main shark on Shark Tank, and runs bridge-building nonprofits such as Starts With Us and Builders.
interesting_fact: As a teen and student he bought watches wholesale and resold them at flea markets and mall kiosks, and wrote a 268-page Trinity University senior thesis on achieving Arab-Israeli peace through business ventures.
deep_cut_fact: His first peace-through-business venture began in 1992 when, as a fresh Stanford Law graduate on a fellowship in Israel, he fell for a sun-dried tomato spread and visited its maker, Yoel Benesh; PeaceWorks later sold it as 'Spraté' under the joke label 'Moshe Pupik & Ali Mishmunken's World Famous Sauces'.
notes: Very accessible: has his own podcast and a published media/speaking inbox (comms@lubetzky.org) - best route. Strong entrepreneurship fit.

name: Manfredi Lefebvre d'Ovidio
current_role: President, Heritage Group (Monaco); Executive Chairman, Abercrombie & Kent Travel Group; Chair, World Travel & Tourism Council (since Sept 2025)
profile: Rome-born, Monaco-based travel magnate who ran his father's Silversea Cruises from 2001, grew it to 12 ships and sold it to Royal Caribbean in 2018-2020 for ~$1.25bn. Then bought 85% of Abercrombie & Kent (2019) and added Crystal Cruises, Cox & Kings and Ecoventura; also backed quantum-encryption firm Arqit and chairs the WTTC.
interesting_fact: Since January 2024 he has been the Sovereign Order of Malta's Ambassador at Large for Culture and Philanthropy and its Permanent Observer to UNESCO.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Silversea, in the 1980s he and his father, Professor Antonio Lefebvre d'Ovidio, bought Sitmar Cruises and built three cruise ships before selling the line to P&O Princess. He also studied law in Rome but left before taking his degree.

public_contacts.value: jtreacy@abercrombiekent.com (James Treacy, Global Communications Director, A&K)
JFawcett@abercrombiekent.com (Jean Fawcett, Senior Manager, Media Relations, A&K)

notes: Frequent conference speaker (WTTC, Skift Forum); approachable via A&K global communications. Arqit stake gives a tech angle.

name: Phongthep Chiaravanont
current_role: Vice Chairman, Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF); Director & Senior Vice Chairman, CP Group; Chairman & CEO, Perfect Companion Group
profile: Member of Thailand's Chearavanont family (cousin of CP Group's Dhanin Chearavanont) and a CPF director since January 1994, now vice chairman. Holds a master's in avian sciences from UC Davis, fitting CP's poultry-and-feed roots, and also chairs the group's pet-food arm Perfect Companion.
interesting_fact: He trained as a poultry scientist, earning a master's degree in avian sciences at the University of California, Davis.
deep_cut_fact: He is Chairman and CEO of Perfect Companion Group, the CP-affiliated pet-food maker behind brands such as SmartHeart and Me-O.
notes: Very low public profile (age ~74). Company-level contacts only. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes.

name: Langley Walker
profile: Most likely Lang (Langley) Walker, co-founder of Sydney property developer Walker Corporation (listed as US in the source data, but Walker Corporation is Australian). He died on 27 January 2024, aged 78.
notes: Deceased (source: https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-01-28/property-developer-lang-walker-dies/103398278 ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walker_Corporation). Country field 'United States' in input appears to be a data error. Identity marked uncertain because of the country mismatch; the source of wealth matches.

name: Li Zuoyuan (李佐元)
profile: Born 1948, a Hong Kong resident (with New Zealand permanent residency) who left state carmaker Dongfeng in 1988 to start his own business, founding Shiyan Changyuan in 1993 and Changyuan Donggu in 2001. The Xiangyang, Hubei company makes cylinder blocks, heads and connecting rods for diesel, natural-gas and gasoline engines plus heat-exchange systems and power units; listed in Shanghai in May 2020.
interesting_fact: Beyond the listed company he is vice chairman of a Cummins power joint venture (康明斯动力) and chairs several affiliated engine-component and heating companies.
deep_cut_fact: He began as an engineer at Dongfeng Motor's No. 2 Foundry (1979-83) and then headed its production and engineering department until 1988, before going out on his own.
notes: Very low international profile; outreach would need to be in Chinese via the board secretary (Liu Wangcheng). Engine/power-unit business has a possible backup-power angle, not verified. Web search budget ran out; details from exchange-disclosure data on Sina Finance.

name: Marilyn Carlson Nelson
current_role: Co-owner and former Chairman & CEO, Carlson (Minnesota hospitality/travel group)
profile: Daughter of Carlson founder Curt Carlson; joined the board in 1973 and became CEO after his 1999 death, running a travel empire spanning Radisson hotels, Regent Seven Seas Cruises, TGI Fridays and Carlson Wagonlit Travel. Handed the chair to her daughter Diana Nelson in 2013 and co-owns the company with her sister; she is now in her late 80s.
interesting_fact: She sat on the board of ExxonMobil (from 1991) and received the Oslo Business for Peace Award in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: A ballerina in her youth, she once flew in a US Air Force Thunderbirds F-16, pulling about 9G while filming a teamwork message for staff, and rollerbladed onto the stage at a 1995 Las Vegas company meeting waving the Carlson flag.
notes: Alive per Wikipedia (no death recorded); recent activity not verified because web search budget ran out. Largely retired; route via Carlson communications.
